frameworks.name: LangChain
frameworks.what_it_is: Python and JS framework for LLM apps
frameworks.verdict: Still the default résumé keyword and a common base for internal RAG chatbots. Users say it works but adds overhead and latency, and some builders advertise skipping it entirely.
frameworks.notes: 11 of 16 snippets are Who-wants-to-be-hired stack lists. Bloat complaints also appear under other tools (49820007 in Pydantic AI, 48658839 in Strands).

frameworks.name: Microsoft Agent Framework
frameworks.what_it_is: Microsoft's open-source .NET and Python agent framework
frameworks.verdict: Shows up mostly in .NET and Azure shops, in job posts and as the C# answer for MCP-based agents. Few hands-on reviews; one commenter notes its harness is still single-player.
frameworks.notes: 5 false matches on generic 'agent framework' (ReAct, Clarity Agent, personal subagent frameworks). No substantive complaints found.

frameworks.name: Claude Agent SDK
frameworks.what_it_is: Anthropic's SDK exposing the Claude Code harness
frameworks.verdict: Most discussion is about billing: whether it can run on a Claude subscription, which the docs now confirm. Builders note it inherits Claude Code's heavy system prompts, and telemetry takes hacks.
frameworks.notes: 2 false matches (Pi coding agent SDK, OpenAI agent SDK). Little direct praise or criticism of the API itself.

frameworks.name: Mastra
frameworks.what_it_is: Open-source TypeScript framework for AI agents
frameworks.verdict: The TypeScript agent framework with the warmest comments. A heavy user runs production agents on it, and a bug reporter says the CTO fixed eval scoring bugs within nine hours.
frameworks.notes: 50377455 appears twice (ask_hn and hn_comment). Several neutral hits are Mastra's own job posts and résumés.

frameworks.name: LangGraph
frameworks.what_it_is: Graph-based agent orchestration library from LangChain
frameworks.verdict: Mostly a résumé keyword next to LangChain. Where people describe it, they reach for it when they want deterministic, graph-shaped control over multi-step agent workflows.
frameworks.notes: Thin evidence: all 13 snippets are neutral, nearly all résumé stack lists. A DSPy-thread comment (49879489) says pure agent loops beat LangGraph-built agents in their evals.

frameworks.name: DSPy
frameworks.what_it_is: Stanford framework for programming and optimizing LLM prompts
frameworks.verdict: Loved by a vocal few for small classification and extraction tasks done in a few lines. Skeptics say plain agent loops beat DSPy-built agents in their own evals.
frameworks.notes: Top HN story is literally 'If DSPy is so great, why isn't anyone using it?'. Debate is about whether its optimization techniques still matter with newer models.

frameworks.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
frameworks.verdict: Common in résumés and enterprise orchestrators. The one detailed user report praises it for wiring sandbox, Slack and knowledge-base integrations while controlling exactly what gets exposed to OpenAI.
frameworks.notes: 1 false match (generic 'an agents sdk'). Several duplicate résumé posts from the same person.

frameworks.name: Google ADK
frameworks.verdict: Google's agent kit, used for sequential and looping multi-agent setups. It ships features fast enough to obsolete in-house work, but its LiteLLM dependency drew complaints after LiteLLM's vulnerability.

frameworks.name: CrewAI
frameworks.what_it_is: Python framework for role-based multi-agent crews
frameworks.verdict: An early multi-agent framework that now shows up mainly as a résumé keyword. The one experience report says agents left to coordinate themselves collaborate awkwardly unless the spec defines roles.
frameworks.notes: Thin evidence: 11 of 12 snippets are stack lists or job posts.

frameworks.name: Pydantic AI
frameworks.what_it_is: Type-safe Python agent framework from Pydantic
frameworks.verdict: A Python favourite among people leaving LangChain. Users like its provider abstractions on their own and use it as a thin base for small headless agents.

frameworks.name: MCP SDKs
frameworks.what_it_is: Official SDKs for building MCP servers and clients
frameworks.verdict: In practice this means FastMCP: a one-line import for wrapping APIs as MCP servers. Complaints are deployment gotchas like localhost-only DNS rebinding defaults, and doubts that MCP beats plain OpenAPI.
frameworks.notes: Every snippet matched on FastMCP; none discuss the official TypeScript or other-language SDKs.

frameworks.name: Vercel AI SDK
frameworks.what_it_is: TypeScript toolkit for LLM apps and streaming
frameworks.verdict: The default TypeScript LLM toolkit in résumés and provider integrations, with its stream protocol ported as far as Ruby. Comments describe usage, not opinions.
frameworks.notes: No evaluative comments; all 12 are neutral mentions (mostly résumés, one chess demo using experimental_evaluate, one naming gripe).

frameworks.name: Strands Agents
frameworks.verdict: AWS's agent SDK, used with Bedrock for things like log-digging devops agents and a talking Raspberry Pi fish. One user hit a cache TTL issue; another questioned what Strands Harness adds.
frameworks.notes: Two snippets are from a Strands team member (47139402, 47139388).

evals.name: Arize Phoenix
evals.what_it_is: Open-source LLM tracing and eval platform
evals.verdict: Open-source tracing and eval tool people use for LLM-as-judge and production trace analysis. Evidence is thin, and one user found its Claude Code tracing setup heavy.
evals.notes: 14 of 19 snippets are false matches (generic Ask HN text about summarizing, none about Phoenix). Real signal is 5 snippets.

evals.name: OpenTelemetry GenAI
evals.what_it_is: OpenTelemetry semantic conventions for LLM telemetry
evals.verdict: The plumbing under most LLM observability tools rather than something people debate. People instrument API calls so agents can query a local collector, and export LLM traces to vendors like Braintrust.
evals.notes: No snippet names the GenAI semantic conventions specifically; matches are on OpenTelemetry generally. 3 marked false are résumés with no LLM context.

evals.name: Langfuse
evals.what_it_is: Open-source LLM tracing, evals and prompt management
evals.verdict: The default open-source pick for LLM tracing, evals and prompt management, all over résumés. Users note a processing lag on traces, which a reply blames on outdated SDKs, and limited chart customisation.
evals.notes: Top HN story is ClickHouse acquiring Langfuse.

evals.name: promptfoo
evals.what_it_is: Open-source CLI for prompt evals and red-teaming
evals.verdict: The go-to for personal regression evals: people use it to check prompts before switching models and to build benchmarks for their own workflow. Its team has since joined OpenAI.
evals.notes: Two snippets are from the Promptfoo team about Codex Security; top HN story is 'Promptfoo Is Joining OpenAI'.

evals.name: MLflow
evals.what_it_is: Open-source ML lifecycle and experiment tracking platform
evals.verdict: The established ML experiment tracker, now also used for agent tracing. Those who tried MLflow 3's agent observability liked its session capture and metadata like files touched and model used.
evals.notes: 10 of 12 are MLOps résumé or job-post mentions.

evals.name: Logfire
evals.verdict: Pydantic's tracing service, often paired with Pydantic AI. Users call it very helpful for diagnosing agent bugs; one who tried both found it similar to Langfuse but with fewer eval features.
evals.notes: Several snippets are from the Pydantic founder about funding, not product use.

evals.name: Braintrust
evals.what_it_is: Hosted LLM eval and observability platform
evals.verdict: A hosted eval platform that shows up in startup stacks like Curai's. The few opinions call it solid for evals; its top HN story is a confirmed breach.
evals.notes: 2 false matches on 'the HN braintrust'. Breach fact comes from top_hn_story, not comments.

evals.name: Helicone
evals.what_it_is: Open-source LLM gateway and observability proxy
evals.verdict: Known as much for its LLM cost page as its gateway. Self-hosters found almost no setup docs, cost analysis needs your own SQL, and the service is now in maintenance mode.
evals.notes: Users disagree on the cost page: one says it updates instantly (46309137), another felt a lag (48244121).

evals.name: LangSmith
evals.what_it_is: LangChain's hosted tracing and eval service
evals.verdict: LangChain's tracing and eval service, mostly a résumé line next to LangGraph, sometimes the eval harness for production agent systems. The one hands-on report dropped it for adding latency.
evals.notes: Thin evidence: 11 of 12 are résumé stack lists.

evals.name: Opik
evals.what_it_is: Comet's open-source LLM tracing and eval tool
evals.verdict: Comet's open-source LLM tracing and eval tool, with little discussion. Mentions call it useful for LLMOps, and one contributor fixed streaming wrappers that were swallowing exceptions.
evals.notes: Only 5 snippets; two are the same résumé.

evals.name: DeepEval
evals.what_it_is: Open-source Python framework for LLM evals
evals.verdict: A Python eval library used mostly for RAG checks and LLM-as-judge assertions. Advice threads pitch it as the code-first option next to promptfoo's YAML.

evals.name: Inspect AI
evals.what_it_is: UK AISI's open-source LLM evaluation framework
evals.verdict: The UK AI Security Institute's eval framework. HN barely discusses it: one résumé, one PR link, and someone planning to try it alongside promptfoo.
evals.notes: Only 3 snippets. Top HN story (Claypot, a kids' studio) is a false match.

evals.name: garak
evals.verdict: NVIDIA's LLM vulnerability scanner. It appears only in red-teaming tool lists next to PyRIT; most HN hits for the name are about the Star Trek character.
evals.notes: 8 of 11 snippets are about Garak from Deep Space Nine. No hands-on reports.

assistants.name: OpenClaw
assistants.verdict: The personal agent many tried and most have retired. A few keep it for event-driven chores and calendar nudges; the rest cite constant tinkering, crashes after a week and poor local-model support.
assistants.notes: Most snippets come from one Ask HN about current AI stacks; the dominant pattern is 'tried it, went back to Claude Code/Codex'.

assistants.name: Hermes Agent
assistants.what_it_is: Nous Research's open-source persistent personal agent
assistants.verdict: The personal agent with the most loyal users, run on Mac Minis or VPSes, reached via Telegram, often on local models. Detractors cite a dated UI and regressions between updates.
assistants.notes: Several users report switching from OpenClaw to Hermes. Some neutral hits are survey questions quoted back.

assistants.name: Claude Cowork
assistants.what_it_is: Claude's desktop agent for non-coding work
assistants.verdict: Claude's agent for non-coding work, used for email, todos, receipts and business operations, including by non-developers. One complaint: it floods teams with AI slop that reviewers must clean up.

assistants.name: Muse
assistants.verdict: Meta's consumer agent. Fans use it for research, forum scraping and group marketing, but most comments cite privacy incidents, ignored permissions, a 0-day, and slowness.
assistants.notes: 1 false match (Muse Glimmer, a coding model). A few mentions may refer to Muse subscriptions/models rather than the agent and were kept neutral.

assistants.name: n8n
assistants.verdict: The workflow automation tool AI and automation freelancers list on résumés, used for chores like filing tax records and forwarding email. One comment calls its open-core licensing direction a mess.
assistants.notes: Little LLM-specific discussion; mostly résumé stack lists.

assistants.name: Home Assistant + LLM
assistants.what_it_is: Home Assistant's LLM conversation and voice integrations
assistants.verdict: Home Assistant's LLM and voice hooks, often run on local models. People wire it to MCP servers for voice control and EV charging plans, though LLMs can struggle with the unofficial MCP.
assistants.notes: 7 false matches: Home Assistant projects with no LLM in the loop (e-paper, CCTV, ESP32, menu bar) and a generic 'LLM home assistant'.

assistants.name: NanoClaw
assistants.what_it_is: Minimal container-isolated OpenClaw alternative in TypeScript
assistants.verdict: A lightweight, container-isolated OpenClaw alternative some find easier to understand. Several users moved on to Hermes or hand-rolled agents, and one ditched it as useless for email triage.

assistants.name: nanobot
assistants.verdict: An ultra-lightweight open-source alternative to OpenClaw from HKUDS. None of the matched HN comments discuss it; every hit is about sci-fi nanobots.
assistants.notes: All 12 snippets are false matches (Kurzweil, grey goo, killer nanobots). Verdict is from the tool's stated purpose and top HN story only; no evidence id supports it.

assistants.name: Duet
assistants.what_it_is: Anthropic's proactive agent for professionals, in preview
assistants.verdict: Anthropic's waitlisted proactive agent, still in research preview. Early users run it for monitoring communications, but find it slow and say OpenAI's Dots is better today.
assistants.notes: Listed url is duet.so but all evidence and the top HN story are about Claude Duet; check the url. Most commenters have not used it yet. Several snippets duplicated.

assistants.name: Eigent
assistants.what_it_is: Open-source desktop alternative to Claude Cowork
assistants.verdict: An open-source desktop alternative to Claude Cowork. HN evidence is effectively nil: one bare link, with every other match being German 'eigentlich' or EigenTrust.
assistants.notes: 11 of 12 false matches. Verdict relies on the tool's stated purpose.

assistants.name: Dots
assistants.verdict: OpenAI's persistent personal agent. One user built a speculative Lean-verified proof with a Dots swarm, another rates it above Duet; critics dislike the cutesy branding and a confusing product lineup.
assistants.notes: Top HN story asks whether Dots intercepts SSL; no snippet discusses that. 50173771 reads like marketing copy.

assistants.name: Paperclip
assistants.what_it_is: Open-source org chart for running agent companies
assistants.verdict: An open-source tool for running a 'company' of agents with an org chart. HN mentions are passing comparisons, with no hands-on reports.

assistants.name: Claude Code Routines
assistants.what_it_is: Scheduled, cloud-run Claude Code agent jobs
assistants.verdict: Scheduled Claude Code jobs, essentially agent cron. People see it as a cheaper subscription path for PR review bots, but several say a local cron job does the same.
assistants.notes: Several neutral snippets are competitors pitching alternatives. One notes overlap with Cowork's scheduled tasks (47770796).
